std-pad-lock.name: std-pad-lock
std-pad-lock.description: Headless pad-lock mechanic: floor pads that light when the player steps on them, completing a set when every pad is lit. Listens BODY_MOVED and lights any unlit live pad the player's rect touches (|dx| <= reachX, |dy| <= reachY of the pad center); a lit pad stays lit. Pads may carry a group number (grp 0 = ungrouped, always live): when groups are used, only pads of the lowest uncompleted group are live — pads of later groups refuse to light until the current group finishes, so one sum must be finished before the next. When a group completes the trait emits PAD_GROUP_COMPLETED once for it (first newly completed group reports; the shared entity carries the rest); when every pad in the set is lit it stamps completed and emits PAD_SET_COMPLETED once. The lowest uncompleted group is stamped on the shared entity as currentGrp so boards can pulse exactly the live pads (0 = no group open / ungrouped pads). RESTART unlights every pad and resets the set. Renders nothing; boards draw the pads and read lit from the shared entity (the render authority). Corresponds to the design-sheet field(s): challenge, mechanics.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Pads
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per floor pad: id, center (x, y in world units), and grp (0 = ungrouped, always live; N = live only while it is the lowest uncompleted group). lit is stamped at runtime.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach X
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal tolerance (world units) around a pad's center when testing player contact (approximates the body's half-width plus a step).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Vertical tolerance (world units) around a pad's center when testing player contact (covers skating over the surface the pad sits on).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, BODY_MOVED lights touched live pads and reports group/set completion; toggle to freeze every pad as-is.

events.name: PAD_GROUP_COMPLETED
events.description: Every pad of one group is lit; fires once per group, in group order — later groups stay dead until the lowest uncompleted group finishes. Boards layer a small fx and unlock the next group's pads.

events.name: PAD_SET_COMPLETED
events.description: Every pad in the set is lit; fires once per run. Boards layer the treasure fx and spill the bonus reward.

std-patience.name: std-patience
std-patience.description: Headless customer-service mechanic: owns a stationary customer roster with per-customer patience. Decrements patience every tick, serves nearby customers on HERO_STEPPED (resets their patience + scores), and emits CUSTOMER_LOST when a timer expires. Never writes units.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Customers
overridableConfigKeys.description: Seed roster of stationary customers, each with their own position + patience/maxPatience

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, patience ticks down and HERO_STEPPED serves nearby customers; toggle to freeze

overridableConfigKeys.label: Serve Radius
overridableConfigKeys.description: Manhattan distance at which a customer counts as served by the hero's last step: 0 = step onto tile, 1 = adjacent

events.name: BURST
events.description: Serve or starve particle burst; a fx-particles listener spawns it

events.name: SERVICE_CHANGED
events.description: Served/pending/lost counts after this step; a market-flow listener decides win/lose

events.name: CUSTOMER_LOST
events.description: Emitted when one or more customers' patience expires in the same tick

std-patrol-hazard.name: std-patrol-hazard
std-patrol-hazard.description: Headless patrol-hazard mechanic for side-view boards: moves each configured patrol back and forth along its [x0, x1] beat at its own speed (33ms tick, ping-pong with clamped turnarounds; a patrol declaring waveAmp/wavePeriod also bobs vertically — cy = y + waveAmp·sin(2πt/wavePeriod from a per-row time accumulator — and the hit test and render read cy, so a waveAmp of 0 keeps the flat beat), tracks the player position off the body authority's BODY_MOVED, and emits PATROL_HIT once per contact — a per-patrol hit flag re-arms only after the player separates, so damage rules stay sparse (when two patrols connect on the same tick the first reports; the other reports on the next tick). Patrols live on a [runtime, shared] entity for the render layer (boards draw them as markers/sprites); damage, lives, and respawn stay downstream (std-lives) — this atom simulates, it never judges. Renders nothing. Corresponds to the design-sheet field(s): challenge, dynamics.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Hit Radius
overridableConfigKeys.description: Per-axis distance (world units) within which a patrol counts as touching the player; smaller values demand precise contact, larger values forgive.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Patrols
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per patroller: id, the [x0, x1] beat it walks, its base y, its speed in units/s, and optionally waveAmp/wavePeriod for a vertical sine bob (waveAmp 0 = flat ping-pong). Current x/dir/t/cy/touching/hit are stamped at runtime.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Player Spawn X
overridableConfigKeys.description: Player x assumed before the first BODY_MOVED arrives (match the body authority's spawn).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Player Spawn Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Player y assumed before the first BODY_MOVED arrives.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the 33ms tick moves patrols and tests contact; toggle to freeze every patrol in place.

events.name: PATROL_HIT
events.description: A patrol made contact with the player this tick; fires once per contact and re-arms only after separation — boards route it to their damage rule (std-lives DAMAGE).

std-pickup.name: std-pickup
std-pickup.description: Headless side-view collectible authority — the platformer twin of grid std-gather. Listens BODY_MOVED and, when the player touches an uncollected feature (|dx| <= reachX, |dy| <= reachY of the feature center — the coef-pad touch idiom minus the grounded requirement, so airborne pickups work), stamps it collected on the shared entity and emits PICKED once per item (id, kind, position, glyph, message) plus COLLECT{total} with the running count (the event std-gate-lock already consumes). When every feature is collected it emits PICKUP_SET_COMPLETED once. RESTART re-arms every feature and zeroes the count. kind is board-defined vocabulary (star, boost, …) — this atom reports, boards judge. Renders nothing; boards draw the features and read collected from the shared entity. Corresponds to the design-sheet field(s): rewards.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Features
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per collectible: id, center (x, y in world units), board-defined kind (star, boost, …), display glyph and message floated on pickup. collected is stamped at runtime.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach X
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal tolerance (world units) around a feature's center when testing player contact.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Vertical tolerance (world units) around a feature's center when testing player contact; generous values catch fly-through pickups.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, BODY_MOVED collects touched features; toggle to freeze the set as-is.

events.name: PICKED
events.description: The player touched an uncollected feature; carries the feature identity, board-defined kind (star, boost, …), position and display glyph/message. Fires once per feature per run.

events.name: COLLECT
events.description: Running count of collected features after this pickup — the event std-gate-lock consumes to count openings.

events.name: PICKUP_SET_COMPLETED
events.description: Every feature in the set is collected; fires once per run.

std-platformer-body.name: std-platformer-body
std-platformer-body.description: Headless run/jump platformer-physics authority: the SOLE writer of body + fell + hazardId + goalId on side-view boards. Where std-motion-body owns free 2D drift (no collision), this atom owns the platformer contract: every 33ms physics tick it integrates gravity into the body's vertical velocity, steps position in per-second units, and collides the body rect against the config platforms with one-way semantics — a body moving in the gravity direction that overlaps a ground/platform tile lands on its anti-gravity face (vy zeroed, grounded set), while a body moving against gravity passes through, so jumping up through a platform and walking up a staircase both just work. The sign of gravity IS the vertical convention: positive pulls toward +y (screen boards, y down — sprite canvases), negative toward −y (math canvases, y up); jumps always fire against it. Intents: STEER sets horizontal velocity (dir −1/0/1 × moveSpeed, hold-to-run: keydown steers, keyup steers 0), JUMP kicks vertical velocity when grounded, PLACE teleports (spawns, hazard respawns), RESTART reseeds. Emits BODY_MOVED every tick for the render layer (boards that don't subscribe pay nothing), plus the sparse rule signals a board needs to score: BODY_JUMPED, BODY_LANDED (with impact speed), BODY_HAZARD (once per hazard entry, re-arms on exit), BODY_GOAL (same arming), BODY_FELL (once per fall past killY, re-armed by PLACE/RESTART). Drift regions: config.driftRegions lists axis-aligned rects each carrying a constant acceleration (ax, ay) applied with the same 0.033s dt whenever the body's center is inside (empty list = zero behavior change). Curve skating: when config.skate is on and the grounded body comes within skateSnap of the config.skateCurve surface, the body rides the curve — y snaps to the interpolated surface and tangential gravity (g·slope/(1+slope²)) accelerates vx, and the vertical velocity is the tangential projection (s = vx·cos θ, vy = s·sin θ — no discontinuous jumps at sample boundaries), so the body slides downhill along the graph itself and launches ballistically off its ends; jumping kicks free. Sparse BODY_SKATE_START/BODY_SKATE_END signals fire on engage/disengage so boards can layer fx. Lives, score, and win/lose stay downstream — this atom simulates, it never judges. Renders nothing. Corresponds to the design-sheet field(s): mechanics, dynamics.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Curve Mods Enabled
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, entity.curveMods reshape the skate surface inside each mod's x-range: the road samples the base curve at b·(x − h) and applies a·y + k (slope scales by a·b) — coefficient pads lift/tilt/compress the segment the player is riding. Multiple overlapping mods stack by summing each mod's delta from the base surface; a mod whose shifted sample leaves the curve range is skipped. Default off: boards without coef pads pay nothing.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Drift Regions
overridableConfigKeys.description: Axis-aligned rects (x0..x1, y0..y1 in world units) each carrying a constant acceleration (ax, ay in units/s²) applied with the physics dt whenever the body's center is inside — winds, currents, gradient pushes. Empty list = zero behavior change.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Gravity
overridableConfigKeys.description: Units/s² added to vertical velocity; the SIGN is the vertical convention — positive pulls toward +y (screen boards, y down), negative toward −y (math canvases, y up) — and jumps always fire against it

overridableConfigKeys.label: Jump Strength
overridableConfigKeys.description: Vertical speed in units/s imparted by JUMP, directed against gravity; apex height ≈ jumpStrength² / (2·|gravity|)

overridableConfigKeys.label: Kill Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Fall line: crossing it in the gravity direction fires BODY_FELL once (past it downward on y-down boards, below it on y-up canvases); y-up consumers must set a value below their world floor

overridableConfigKeys.label: Max Fall Speed
overridableConfigKeys.description: Terminal velocity cap in units/s applied to vertical speed each tick

overridableConfigKeys.label: Move Speed
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal run speed in units/s applied by STEER dir ±1

overridableConfigKeys.label: Platforms
overridableConfigKeys.description: Level geometry as min-corner rects: ground/platform tiles are solid one-way landing surfaces, hazard tiles emit BODY_HAZARD on touch, goal tiles emit BODY_GOAL

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the 33ms physics tick integrates and collides; toggle to freeze the body

overridableConfigKeys.label: Curve Skating
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, a grounded body within skateSnap of the skateCurve surface rides the curve: y snaps to the interpolated surface and tangential gravity (g·slope/(1+slope²)) accelerates vx, so the body slides downhill along the graph and launches off its ends; JUMP kicks free. Engages when grounded, when landing on a tile, or when a falling (not rising) body passes within skateSnap above the surface.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Curve
overridableConfigKeys.description: Surface samples (x strictly increasing) the body skates when skate is on; y is the surface height for the body's MIN corner, linearly interpolated between bracketing samples — mirror the render-side curve so what you see is what you ride

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Max Gap
overridableConfigKeys.description: Largest x-gap between consecutive skateCurve samples that still counts as surface. 0 = unlimited (sparse two-sample lines skate fine). Dense resampled curves with real gaps between segments (stitched worlds) MUST set this — otherwise the sampler invents a skatable chord across every gap (an invisible line above the bridge/terrain that the body snaps to and glides along).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Snap
overridableConfigKeys.description: Max vertical gap (world units) between the body's min corner and the curve surface for skating to engage or stay engaged; larger values grab earlier on landing, smaller values release sooner on bumps

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Body
overridableConfigKeys.description: Initial body rect (min-corner x/y plus width/height) seeded on INIT/RESTART; width/height also define the collision box

overridableConfigKeys.label: Right Wall
overridableConfigKeys.description: Largest x the body's min corner may hold (world bounds, not level geometry)

overridableConfigKeys.label: Left Wall
overridableConfigKeys.description: Smallest x the body's min corner may hold (world bounds, not level geometry)

events.name: BODY_MOVED
events.description: The body after this physics tick: position, velocity, grounded and skating flags, and scalar speed; render layers subscribe (or read the shared entity), rule layers stay on the sparse signals

events.name: BODY_SKATE_START
events.description: Body engaged curve skating this tick (grounded, landing, or falling within skateSnap above the skateCurve surface); slope is the local dy/dx — boards layer fx and equation readouts

events.name: BODY_SKATE_END
events.description: Body left the curve surface (jumped, walked past an end, or drifted beyond skateSnap); boards tear down skate fx

events.name: BODY_JUMPED
events.description: Jump accepted (grounded at intent time) and vertical velocity kicked against gravity; boards layer squash/sound fx

events.name: BODY_LANDED
events.description: Body transitioned airborne → standing on a ground/platform tile this tick; impact is the pre-landing fall speed in units/s so boards can scale dust or damage

events.name: BODY_HAZARD
events.description: Body entered overlap with a hazard tile; fires once per entry and re-arms only after the body leaves, so damage rules stay sparse

events.name: BODY_GOAL
events.description: Body entered overlap with a goal tile; fires once per entry and re-arms only after the body leaves — the board's win-rule trigger

events.name: BODY_FELL
events.description: Body crossed killY in the gravity direction (pit fall); fires once per fall and re-arms on PLACE/RESTART, leaving the respawn rule to the board

events.name: CURVE_MOD_CLEAR
events.description: Curve mods were cleared; the skate surface is back to the base skateCurve until a new mod is added.

std-production.name: std-production
std-production.description: Headless unit-production mechanic: accrues productionPoints each turn (AI_TURN) and, on an affordable PRODUCE, emits a SPAWN intent for the grid-tactics authority to place a new unit. Owns only productionPoints (+ its spawn counter); never writes units directly.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Points Per Turn
overridableConfigKeys.description: Points accrued each AI_TURN (turn advance).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, turns accrue points and PRODUCE spends them; toggle to freeze production.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Cost
overridableConfigKeys.description: Points spent per produced unit; PRODUCE only fires when affordable.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Health
overridableConfigKeys.description: Health/maxHealth of produced units.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Team
overridableConfigKeys.description: Team of produced units.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Unit Type
overridableConfigKeys.description: unitType of produced units (drives the asset-manifest sprite).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn X
overridableConfigKeys.description: Grid column where produced units appear (rally point).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Grid row where produced units appear (rally point).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Start Points
overridableConfigKeys.description: Production points set on INIT.

events.name: SPAWN
events.description: New-unit intent applied by the grid-tactics authority (the sole units writer)

std-round-flow.name: std-round-flow
std-round-flow.description: Headless win/lose round-resolution mechanic: derives result (victory/defeat/none) from team survivor counts on each UNITS_CHANGED signal and emits GAME_END. Owns only result; boards own their own phase/turn. Renders nothing.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, incoming unit-count changes are evaluated for win/lose; toggle to freeze.

events.name: GAME_END
events.description: Called when the round resolves to a win or loss

std-score.name: std-score
std-score.description: Headless scoring mechanic: awards points when the enemy survivor count drops on a UNITS_CHANGED signal. Owns only score (+ its kill baseline); renders nothing.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Initial Enemies
overridableConfigKeys.description: Enemy count at start; the kill baseline so the first kill scores correctly.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Points Per Kill
overridableConfigKeys.description: Points awarded for each enemy removed since the last signal.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, enemy-count drops award points; toggle to freeze scoring.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Start Score
overridableConfigKeys.description: Initial score set on INIT.

std-survival-flow.name: std-survival-flow
std-survival-flow.description: Headless win/lose authority for the nature-survival board: owns only result. Listens RESOURCES (movesLeft) and sets result to lost when the move budget runs out before the camp is built; listens BUILD_CAMP (the render-gated win intent) and sets result to won. Renders nothing.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, RESOURCES/BUILD_CAMP signals resolve win/lose; toggle to freeze

events.name: GAME_END
events.description: Emitted once the match resolves to won or lost

std-svg-asset-art.name: std-svg-asset-art
std-svg-asset-art.description: SvgAssetArtCollector — SOLE writer of @entity.svgAssetArt: collects vector asset catalogs published on the bus (SVG_ASSET_PUBLISH { kind, states }) into one kind → (state → draw-group items) map that board frames select per-row per anim state. INIT seeds from config and emits SVG_ASSET_SYNC so already-mounted catalogs republish regardless of mount order; the SYNC self-hop re-applies the seed after sibling canvas stashes exist (Almadar_Runtime_Gaps.md R-INIT-SEED-REPAINT-RACE). Renders nothing — render authority stays with the frame.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Seed Art
overridableConfigKeys.description: Initial kind → (state → draw-group items) catalog merged under bus-published entries (published entries win). Lets a board ship vector art with zero asset imports.

events.name: SVG_ASSET_SYNC
events.description: Asks mounted svg asset catalogs to (re)publish their states; also the collector's own seed re-apply hop

std-tutorial-autodemo.name: std-tutorial-autodemo
std-tutorial-autodemo.description: Generic scripted input-replay atom: the demo half of a tutorial. Holds one or more named cue scripts (each an ordered list of { at, event, arg } rows where at is a millisecond offset and event is LEFT/RIGHT/JUMP/STOP); listens for TUTORIAL_DEMO_START { demoId } (from std-tutorial-overlay's demoId step) and plays the matching script on a 32ms clock, emitting the semantic DEMO_LEFT / DEMO_RIGHT / DEMO_JUMP / DEMO_STOP events the host board maps onto its own movement. TUTORIAL_DEMO_STOP, DEMO_CANCEL (real user input), or exhausting the cue list end the demo and emit DEMO_STOP so the character stops moving. Renders a small Demo badge while playing. Domain-agnostic: the demo never emits board events (OW_*, etc.) — the organism maps DEMO_* to its own steering, so a demo cannot self-cancel through the board's input path.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Scripts
overridableConfigKeys.description: Named cue scripts keyed by the tutorial step's demoId; each cue fires its event after `at` milliseconds of the demo clock.

events.name: DEMO_LEFT
events.description: Scripted run-left cue; the host board maps this to its own steer-left.

events.name: DEMO_RIGHT
events.description: Scripted run-right cue; the host board maps this to its own steer-right.

events.name: DEMO_JUMP
events.description: Scripted jump cue; the host board maps this to its own jump.

events.name: DEMO_STOP
events.description: Scripted stop cue (or demo end/cancel); the host board maps this to stop movement.

events.name: TUTORIAL_DEMO_START
events.description: A tutorial step carrying a demoId was shown (std-tutorial-overlay); begin playing the cue script whose id matches demoId.

events.name: TUTORIAL_DEMO_STOP
events.description: The tutorial left a demo step or was dismissed; stop the demo and release control.

events.name: DEMO_CANCEL
events.description: Real user input was received by the host board; stop the demo immediately and hand control back to the player.

std-tutorial-overlay.name: std-tutorial-overlay
std-tutorial-overlay.description: Tutorial modal with live-demo steps for game boards and learning shells: a paged overlay — title, a live previewTrait frame playing the mechanic via std-tutorial-autodemo (a bare game canvas, no shell chrome), one line of body copy, a step counter, and Back / Next / Skip — composed entirely from registered render types (stack + text + button + trait frame) into the overlay slot, so no new UI component is needed. autoShow opens it on INIT for first-time players; a board's help button re-opens it any time via SHOW (which rewinds to step one). DISMISS (or finishing the last step) marks the run done, clears the overlay, and emits TUTORIAL_DONE so the board can unpause or log. Steps are pure config — a board teaches a new mechanic by adding one { id, title, body, demoId } row plus a previewTrait binding. Corresponds to the design-sheet field(s): feedback, agency.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Auto Show
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the tutorial opens on INIT for this run; when false it stays hidden until SHOW.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Preview trait
overridableConfigKeys.description: Trait rendered in the media position of the modal — the live, demo-driven preview of the mechanic (a bare game canvas, no shell chrome). '@trait.TutorialEmptyPreview' leaves the slot blank. Override with '@trait.<TraitName>' to show a board's live frame.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Steps
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per tutorial page: title, one line of body copy, and an optional demoId that plays a scripted live demo (std-tutorial-autodemo) for the mechanic being taught.

events.name: TUT_AUTO
events.description: Self-emitted on INIT when autoShow is on — opens step one. (A config-valued INIT guard would be constant-folded at compose time and misfire; the self-event keeps the decision in an effect.)

events.name: TUT_NEXT
events.description: Advance one step; on the last step it finishes the tutorial (marks done, clears the overlay, emits TUTORIAL_DONE).

events.name: TUT_BACK
events.description: Return one step (inert on the first).

events.name: TUT_DISMISS
events.description: Skip/close the tutorial; marks done and clears the overlay.

events.name: SHOW
events.description: Re-open the tutorial from step one — wire a board's help button here.

events.name: TUTORIAL_DONE
events.description: The tutorial was finished or skipped; boards unpause or log completion.

events.name: TUTORIAL_DEMO_START
events.description: Emitted when a tutorial step carrying a demoId is shown; the composed std-tutorial-autodemo atom plays that scripted demo.

events.name: TUTORIAL_DEMO_STOP
events.description: Emitted when the tutorial leaves a demo step (next/back) or is dismissed/finished; the autodemo atom stops and releases control.

std-velocity-gate.name: std-velocity-gate
std-velocity-gate.description: Headless velocity-gate mechanic: gates that open only when the player crosses them inside a speed band, optionally in a required direction, optionally sustained for a dwell. Listens BODY_MOVED and, per closed gate, tests the player's rect (padded by reachMargin), their speed against [minSpeed, maxSpeed], and their horizontal direction against dir (0 = either). Instant gates (dwellMs 0) open on the first passing cross; dwell gates (dwellMs > 0) accumulate ~33ms per passing move and open once held reaches dwellMs — a failing move resets the hold. The first newly opened gate emits VELOCITY_GATE_OPENED (the shared entity carries the rest). Entering a closed INSTANT gate while NOT passing emits VELOCITY_GATE_DENIED once per approach — re-arming only after the player steps out — so the board can answer with a PLACE back and a hint fx; dwell gates never deny (a hot entry is fine — coming to rest inside is the point), a failed hold simply resets. RESTART re-closes every gate. Renders nothing; boards draw the gate band/chest and read open/held from the shared entity (the render authority). Corresponds to the design-sheet field(s): challenge, mechanics.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Gates
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per velocity gate: id, min-corner rect (x, y, width, height in world units), the speed band [minSpeed, maxSpeed] that opens it, the hold required (dwellMs 0 = instant), the horizontal direction required (dir -1/0/+1), and an optional hint shown when denied. open/touching/denied/held/reported are stamped at runtime.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach Margin
overridableConfigKeys.description: Extra world units padded around a closed gate's rect when testing player contact (approximates the body's size).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, BODY_MOVED tests every gate's band and opens/denies; toggle to freeze every gate as-is.

events.name: VELOCITY_GATE_OPENED
events.description: A gate's speed band was satisfied (instantly, or held for its dwell) and it flipped open; boards layer treasure fx and rewards. When several gates open on one move, the first reports and the shared entity carries the rest.

events.name: VELOCITY_GATE_DENIED
events.description: The player entered a closed gate outside its speed band or against its direction; fires once per approach and re-arms after they step out. Boards answer with a PLACE back plus a hint fx.

std-xp.name: std-xp
std-xp.description: Headless XP/progression mechanic: grants xp when the enemy survivor count drops (UNITS_CHANGED), and on reaching xpToNext levels up — raising the threshold and emitting a HEAL reward the grid-tactics authority applies. Owns only xp/xpToNext/level (+ kill baseline); never writes units.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Base XP To Next
overridableConfigKeys.description: XP threshold for the first level-up.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Heal Team
overridableConfigKeys.description: Team whose units are healed on level-up.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Initial Enemies
overridableConfigKeys.description: Enemy count at start; the kill baseline so the first kill grants xp correctly.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Level-Up Heal
overridableConfigKeys.description: Health restored to the healTeam's units on each level-up.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, enemy-count drops grant xp and trigger level-ups; toggle to freeze.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Start XP
overridableConfigKeys.description: XP set on INIT.

overridableConfigKeys.label: XP Per Kill
overridableConfigKeys.description: XP awarded for each enemy removed since the last signal.

overridableConfigKeys.label: XP To Next Increment
overridableConfigKeys.description: Amount the threshold rises by on each level-up.

events.name: HEAL
events.description: Level-up heal reward applied by the grid-tactics authority (the sole units writer)

std-zone-card.name: std-zone-card
std-zone-card.description: Headless zone-guidance mechanic for side-view boards: tracks which band of the world the player is in and holds up that zone's card — name, concept, objective — for a while after every crossing. Listens BODY_MOVED and, when the player's x crosses into a different config zone, stamps the shared entity (zoneId, card, enteredAt) and emits ZONE_CHANGED carrying the card fields; the card self-clears ttlTicks BODY_MOVED ticks later (a per-move tick counter on the entity, so pauses at speed zero still age it out) and boards clear it early via CARD_DISMISS (renamed to a board-scoped progress event) on any mechanic completion. RESTART clears the card and the clock. Renders nothing; boards draw the card from the shared entity (the render authority).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, BODY_MOVED tracks the current zone and ages the card; toggle to freeze the card as-is.

overridableConfigKeys.label: TTL Ticks
overridableConfigKeys.description: BODY_MOVED ticks the card stays up after a zone crossing (≈ 4s at 30 moves/s) before it clears itself.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Zones
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per world band: id, display name, the one-line concept, the zone's objective text, and the x-range (x0..x1) the band covers.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Bone
overridableConfigKeys.description: Skeleton bone name. A named group is addressable by a `draw-mesh` `skin` block (smooth skinning): the skinned mesh deforms with this group's animated transform. Names resolve within the nearest enclosing `skeleton: true` group (falling back to the canvas), so multiple instances of one rig never collide. Distinct from `id` (the hit-test handle).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Clip
overridableConfigKeys.description: Clip the group's items to an SVG path (`d` syntax) in world units relative to the group origin — masked reveals, meters, portraits.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Rotation
overridableConfigKeys.description: Euler rotation `[x, y, z]` in radians (world axes) — per-axis joint rotation for the 3D backend; a group placed at a joint with children authored joint-local IS a bone. The 2D painter applies only the in-plane `z` component, after `rotate`.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Scale
overridableConfigKeys.description: Uniform scale applied to the whole group.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skeleton
overridableConfigKeys.description: Marks this group as a skeleton SCOPE: `bone` names and `skin` bindings in its subtree resolve against each other only — one scope per rig instance.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Tube

overridableConfigKeys.label: Uvs

std-platformer-board-2d.name: std-platformer-board-2d
std-platformer-board-2d.description: 2D run/jump platformer board FRAME: composes platformer-body (run/jump physics, one-way AABB collision, hazard/goal/fall signals) + fx-particles + objective-flow (win/lose gate) onto one shared GameState with a side-view canvas render. The intent trait owns only game RULES — input forwarding (LEFT/RIGHT/STOP/JUMP → STEER/JUMP intents), goal scoring, hazard/pit lives with respawn, PLAY_AGAIN reset — physics, particles, and the win gate belong to the atoms. Games consume this organism and supply level geometry (platforms, in both BodyAuthority.platforms for collision and the render-side platforms knob), theme/assets, and physics feel via config/traitOverrides.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Curve Mods Enabled
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, entity.curveMods reshape the skate surface inside each mod's x-range: the road samples the base curve at b·(x − h) and applies a·y + k (slope scales by a·b) — coefficient pads lift/tilt/compress the segment the player is riding. Multiple overlapping mods stack by summing each mod's delta from the base surface; a mod whose shifted sample leaves the curve range is skipped. Default off: boards without coef pads pay nothing.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Drift Regions
overridableConfigKeys.description: Axis-aligned rects (x0..x1, y0..y1 in world units) each carrying a constant acceleration (ax, ay in units/s²) applied with the physics dt whenever the body's center is inside — winds, currents, gradient pushes. Empty list = zero behavior change.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Gravity
overridableConfigKeys.description: Units/s² added to vertical velocity; the SIGN is the vertical convention — positive pulls toward +y (screen boards, y down), negative toward −y (math canvases, y up) — and jumps always fire against it

overridableConfigKeys.label: Jump Strength
overridableConfigKeys.description: Vertical speed in units/s imparted by JUMP, directed against gravity; apex height ≈ jumpStrength² / (2·|gravity|)

overridableConfigKeys.label: Kill Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Fall line: crossing it in the gravity direction fires BODY_FELL once (past it downward on y-down boards, below it on y-up canvases); y-up consumers must set a value below their world floor

overridableConfigKeys.label: Max Fall Speed
overridableConfigKeys.description: Terminal velocity cap in units/s applied to vertical speed each tick

overridableConfigKeys.label: Move Speed
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal run speed in units/s applied by STEER dir ±1

overridableConfigKeys.label: Platforms
overridableConfigKeys.description: Level geometry as min-corner rects: ground/platform tiles are solid one-way landing surfaces, hazard tiles emit BODY_HAZARD on touch, goal tiles emit BODY_GOAL

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the 33ms physics tick integrates and collides; toggle to freeze the body

overridableConfigKeys.label: Curve Skating
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, a grounded body within skateSnap of the skateCurve surface rides the curve: y snaps to the interpolated surface and tangential gravity (g·slope/(1+slope²)) accelerates vx, so the body slides downhill along the graph and launches off its ends; JUMP kicks free. Engages when grounded, when landing on a tile, or when a falling (not rising) body passes within skateSnap above the surface.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Curve
overridableConfigKeys.description: Surface samples (x strictly increasing) the body skates when skate is on; y is the surface height for the body's MIN corner, linearly interpolated between bracketing samples — mirror the render-side curve so what you see is what you ride

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Max Gap
overridableConfigKeys.description: Largest x-gap between consecutive skateCurve samples that still counts as surface. 0 = unlimited (sparse two-sample lines skate fine). Dense resampled curves with real gaps between segments (stitched worlds) MUST set this — otherwise the sampler invents a skatable chord across every gap (an invisible line above the bridge/terrain that the body snaps to and glides along).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Snap
overridableConfigKeys.description: Max vertical gap (world units) between the body's min corner and the curve surface for skating to engage or stay engaged; larger values grab earlier on landing, smaller values release sooner on bumps

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Body
overridableConfigKeys.description: Initial body rect (min-corner x/y plus width/height) seeded on INIT/RESTART; width/height also define the collision box

overridableConfigKeys.label: Move Speed
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal run speed in units/s applied by STEER dir ±1

overridableConfigKeys.label: Platforms
overridableConfigKeys.description: Level geometry as min-corner rects: ground/platform tiles are solid one-way landing surfaces, hazard tiles emit BODY_HAZARD on touch, goal tiles emit BODY_GOAL

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the 33ms physics tick integrates and collides; toggle to freeze the body

overridableConfigKeys.label: Curve Skating
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, a grounded body within skateSnap of the skateCurve surface rides the curve: y snaps to the interpolated surface and tangential gravity (g·slope/(1+slope²)) accelerates vx, so the body slides downhill along the graph and launches off its ends; JUMP kicks free. Engages when grounded, when landing on a tile, or when a falling (not rising) body passes within skateSnap above the surface.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Curve
overridableConfigKeys.description: Surface samples (x strictly increasing) the body skates when skate is on; y is the surface height for the body's MIN corner, linearly interpolated between bracketing samples — mirror the render-side curve so what you see is what you ride

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Max Gap
overridableConfigKeys.description: Largest x-gap between consecutive skateCurve samples that still counts as surface. 0 = unlimited (sparse two-sample lines skate fine). Dense resampled curves with real gaps between segments (stitched worlds) MUST set this — otherwise the sampler invents a skatable chord across every gap (an invisible line above the bridge/terrain that the body snaps to and glides along).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Skate Snap
overridableConfigKeys.description: Max vertical gap (world units) between the body's min corner and the curve surface for skating to engage or stay engaged; larger values grab earlier on landing, smaller values release sooner on bumps

overridableConfigKeys.label: Spawn Body
overridableConfigKeys.description: Initial body rect (min-corner x/y plus width/height) seeded on INIT/RESTART; width/height also define the collision box

overridableConfigKeys.label: Right Wall
overridableConfigKeys.description: Largest x the body's min corner may hold (world bounds, not level geometry)

overridableConfigKeys.label: Left Wall
overridableConfigKeys.description: Smallest x the body's min corner may hold (world bounds, not level geometry)

overridableConfigKeys.label: Features
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per collectible: id, center (x, y in world units), board-defined kind (star, boost, …), display glyph and message floated on pickup. collected is stamped at runtime.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach X
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal tolerance (world units) around a feature's center when testing player contact.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Vertical tolerance (world units) around a feature's center when testing player contact; generous values catch fly-through pickups.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, BODY_MOVED collects touched features; toggle to freeze the set as-is.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, PROGRESS signals resolve win/lose; toggle to freeze

overridableConfigKeys.label: Choice Gates
overridableConfigKeys.description: One row per gate: id, gate center (x, y — y is the option-platform surface the judge tests against), the hint floated on a wrong answer, and the options: id, dx offset from the gate center, the label drawn above the platform, and correct. solved/chosen are stamped at runtime.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach X
overridableConfigKeys.description: Horizontal tolerance (world units) around an option platform's center when testing a landing (approximates the body's half-width plus a step).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Reach Y
overridableConfigKeys.description: Vertical tolerance (world units) around the gate's option plane when testing a landing (covers small hops onto the platform surface).

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true, BODY_MOVED judges option landings; toggle to freeze every gate as-is.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Decay Rate
overridableConfigKeys.description: Ttl units removed from every fx entry each tick; higher fades particles faster.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Initial Fx
overridableConfigKeys.description: Seed particles rendered before the first BURST; usually empty.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the decay tick runs; toggle to freeze effects.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Running

std-learn-arrangement.name: std-learn-arrangement
std-learn-arrangement.description: Generic build-an-ordering-then-grade instrument — a config-declared roster of items (each with a correct position index and an optional hint) is tapped one at a time from a remaining-items button row onto a growing sequence of ordered slots rendered on a math-canvas; a tapped item becomes unavailable, an Undo button removes the last placement, and once every slot is filled a Check button grades the arrangement with per-slot correct/wrong coloring, a score readout, and a verdict badge. Retry clears the placements and keeps the same roster. Item vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any ordering task (process steps, chronology, procedure, ranking) standalone. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-classify.name: std-learn-classify

std-learn-compare.name: std-learn-compare
std-learn-compare.description: Generic dual-view comparator — two instances of the same config-declared curve family (power y = A·xᴮ, linear y = A + B·x, or sine y = A·sin(B·x)) render overlaid on one canvas, each side driven by its own parameter pair of sliders, with a live delta readout of the two values at the midpoint x. std-learn-coupled-sim.name: std-learn-coupled-sim
std-learn-coupled-sim.description: Generic coupled-dynamics simulation — two named quantities evolve each tick under a config-selected interaction family (predator-prey: dP = aP − bPQ, dQ = cbPQ − dQ; epidemic: dS = −aSI, dI = aSI − bI; kinetics: dP = −aP, dQ = aP − bQ), drawn live as two time-series curves while Run is engaged. The two governing rates are exposed as sliders the learner can retune mid-run, and shock buttons inject or remove a burst of the first quantity so the learner feels how the coupled system absorbs disturbance. All names, coefficients, and scales are config-declared, so one mechanism serves rabbits and foxes, infection and recovery, reactant and product, adopters and churn. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-derivation.name: std-learn-derivation
std-learn-derivation.description: Generic goal-directed derivation/proof-builder instrument — config-declared starting lines (facts and two-sided links) sit in a scrollable derivation panel with per-line badges, a roster of config-declared candidate steps render as buttons, and picking one dynamically matches it against the CURRENT lines (a left/right side of some link plus a same/opposite negation sense) to derive a new line, appending it with config-declared badge styling on success or surfacing a config-declared feedback string on failure; an inline clock can auto-apply the first applicable candidate every autoApplyIntervalMs while running, a Reset restores the starting lines, and the goal is reached when a derived line's label matches the config-declared goal label. Left/right and same/opposite are structural roles, not domain vocabulary, so the same matching mechanism serves propositional inference, chained implications, precursor/product chemistry, or any other two-sided-relation derivation on a biology-canvas-free text panel. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-estimate.name: std-learn-estimate
std-learn-estimate.description: Generic estimation drill — a config-declared prompt roster asks for a quantity, the learner commits an estimate on a slider and locks it in, and the guess is graded by relative-error band: within the exact band scores full points, within the close band partial, outside none, with the true answer and the learner's percentage error revealed after each lock-in and a running score across the round. All vocabulary and bands are config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any quantitative intuition: orders of magnitude, unit conversions, historical dates, population sizes, physical constants, probabilities. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-fx-cues.name: std-learn-fx-cues
std-learn-fx-cues.description: Headless pedagogy→fx translator: rides the bare-event cascade of the graded learning instruments (ANSWER_JUDGED, TAP_JUDGED, ESTIMATE_JUDGED, CLASSIFY_UPDATED, ARRANGEMENT_CHECKED, GOAL_CHECKED, LEARN_ROUND_COMPLETE, TRACE_DONE) and emits BURST cues for std-fx-particles to hold and a composed fx-overlay to play — correct/wrong beats, streak glow at a threshold, and a celebration on completion. Cues are typed FxCue config values carrying their own style (position, ttl, screen effect, color), so a lab opts in with two `uses` lines plus an overlay node and restyles or disables any cue purely through config; the instruments never learn about visuals, and this atom never learns about subjects. std-learn-goal-seek.name: std-learn-goal-seek
std-learn-goal-seek.description: Generic goal-seek (inverse-problem) instrument — a config-declared target curve is drawn from a hidden parameter pair, and the learner tunes their own two parameters with sliders until their curve matches it, then presses Check to be graded against an RMS-distance tolerance. A live distance readout (optionally hidden for a harder variant) plays warmer/colder. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-grid-sim.name: std-learn-grid-sim

The learner seeds the world by tapping cells directly on the canvas, then Runs, Pauses, or single-Steps the evolution, with a generation counter and live active-cell census. Rule, grid dimensions, seeds, and palette are all config-declared, so one mechanism serves emergence, percolation, epidemic fronts, heat flow, and any local-rules-global-behaviour lesson. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-perturb.name: std-learn-perturb
std-learn-perturb.description: Generic equilibrium-and-shock simulation — a single named quantity relaxes each tick toward an adjustable setpoint at an adjustable recovery rate (dV = k·(E − V)), drawn live against the setpoint line. Shock buttons knock the quantity up or down mid-run and the learner watches it recover; moving the setpoint slider mid-run makes the system chase a new equilibrium, and the recovery-rate slider shows sluggish versus snappy regulation. All names and scales are config-declared, so one mechanism serves every negative-feedback lesson: body temperature homeostasis, a thermostat, market price around equilibrium, blood glucose, reservoir level, ecological resilience. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-slope-probe.name: std-learn-slope-probe
std-learn-slope-probe.description: Headless derivative probe for graph-riding learning boards: while the body authority's BODY_MOVED reports its `skating` flag (body riding the curve), it brackets the configured curve around the body's x and derives the local calculus readout — the slope dy/dx, a tangent-line segment of half-width `window` centered on the contact point, a rise-over-run triangle (run `triRun`, rise slope·run), and the glow window of curve samples around the contact — all written to a [runtime, shared] entity so the board renders the math the player is physically riding. Emits the sparse SLOPE_CHANGED signal only when the slope crosses a 0.5 bucket boundary, so fx and HUD meters react to *changes* in steepness without paying a per-tick event. The curve is the same sample table the body skates and the canvas draws — one source, three views. Renders nothing.

overridableConfigKeys.description: Half-length (world units along the tangent) of the tangent segment and of the glow sample window around the contact point.

events.name: SLOPE_CHANGED

std-learn-tour-3d.description: Generic guided-tour-over-3D-stations instrument. Contract: a config-declared roster of stations (id, name, caption, x, y, z, radius, color, shape, opacity) plus optional connector edges (from, to, color, label), rendered as an orbit-rotatable volumetric scene on a biology-canvas in 3D mode; pressing Tour advances the selection to the next station (mod the roster length) and clicking a shape selects its station — either way the camera retargets onto the selected station's x/y/z, the station enlarges, a name — caption narration renders, and a progress readout tracks visited stations until every station has been toured. std-learn-transport.name: std-learn-transport
std-learn-transport.description: Generic 2D step-transport (clock) instrument — the substrate twin of std-learn-sim-3d for discrete-step instruments. Contract: the atom owns the Step/Run-Pause/Reset transport and the clock but NOT the subject computation — STEP advances one step manually, TOGGLE_RUN engages a 32ms tick that accumulates elapsed time and fires one step every stepIntervalMs, RESET zeroes the counters and restores autoRun. Every step (button or clock) broadcasts LEARN_STEP; a composed sibling trait transitions directly on the LEARN_STEP / LEARN_RESET / LEARN_UPDATED broadcasts (the same bare-event cascade the lab routers use), applies the domain computation, halts the clock by setting the shared entity's done flag (the sibling is done's ONLY writer — it must also clear it on LEARN_RESET), and owns the scene render — this atom renders only its control strip and step caption. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Auto Run
overridableConfigKeys.description: When true the clock starts stepping on INIT; the Reset arm restores this value.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Match Mode
overridableConfigKeys.description: When composed behind a lab router, the MODE_SELECTED mode value this instrument responds to. Empty string means standalone — render immediately on INIT.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Step Interval (ms)
overridableConfigKeys.description: Milliseconds of running clock per domain step — the 32ms base tick accumulates elapsed time and fires LEARN_STEP each time this interval elapses. 300-900 suits narrated steppers; 32 fires every frame for continuous sims.

overridableConfigKeys.label: Title
overridableConfigKeys.description: Title shown above the transport controls.

events.name: LEARN_STEP
events.description: Fires once per domain step — from the Step button or every stepIntervalMs of running clock — with the step counter; the composed subject trait transitions on it and applies one step of the domain computation. A harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.

events.name: LEARN_RESET
events.description: Fires on Reset after the transport counters re-zero; the composed subject trait reseeds its domain state from config on it. A harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.

events.name: LEARN_UPDATED
events.description: Fires on INIT/MODE_SELECTED/Run-Pause toggle with the transport state — running flag and step counter — so the composed subject trait can repaint its shell (Run/Pause label, step readout). A harmless no-op when the atom runs standalone.

std-learn-tree.name: std-learn-tree
std-learn-tree.description: Generic ordered-tree builder instrument — inserts values one by one from a config-declared sequence, each value descends left/right by comparison against the current node and attaches as a leaf; the tree renders on algo-graph-canvas (layout: tree, auto-positioned from the parent/child edges), settled nodes green, the descent cursor red, the comparison trail amber. Traverse sweeps the tree to the chosen order (inorder/preorder/levelorder) one node per press or on auto-run, narrating the visit order so far. Vocabulary, sample values, colors, and labels are entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any ordered-tree domain.
